package_info.package_versions: multiple releases, starting in the high 90s for the major version
package_info.why_malicious: Both packages contain obfuscated, hex-encoded payloads that, when decoded and executed, collect sensitive system and user information and exfiltrate it via network requests. The code is intentionally hidden using double hex encoding and dynamic evaluation, which is a strong indicator of malicious intent. The payload performs system reconnaissance and data exfiltration, which is not expected in legitimate helper libraries.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (upon module load or function call)
execution_context.file_location: main entry JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or similar)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code decodes a double hex-encoded payload and executes it using eval, enabling arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the running process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of double hex encoding and dynamic evaluation (eval) to execute hidden code is a classic obfuscation technique used to hide malicious payloads from static analysis and casual inspection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not obfuscate code in this manner or execute dynamically decoded payloads at import-time or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation and dynamic code execution may be used in some DRM or anti-tampering scenarios, but are extremely rare and discouraged in open-source helper libraries.
key_indicators: Dynamic use of eval to execute decoded code
Payload is not human-readable in source
Immediate execution upon import or function call

execution_context.file_location: decoded and executed from main entry file (see snippet_1)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects system information (home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, network interfaces, directory listings) and exfiltrates it via an HTTPS POST request to an external server, enabling system reconnaissance and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs extensive system reconnaissance and exfiltrates the collected data to an external server. This is a hallmark of information-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate helper libraries should not collect or transmit system or user information without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect limited system information, but always with user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Collection of sensitive system and user data
Enumeration of files and directories across multiple OS roots
Exfiltration of data via HTTPS POST
Obfuscated and hidden within a decoded payload

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated payload is loaded and decoded using double hex decoding.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the decoded malicious payload

attack_chain.action: Decoded payload is executed via eval, granting it full access to the Node.js environment.
Malicious payload collects system, user, and network information, and enumerates files and directories.
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive system and user data (final goal)

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated (hex-encoded) payloads decoded and executed at import-time or runtime
Dynamic use of eval on decoded strings
Collection of system, user, and network information without user interaction
Enumeration of root and home directories
Exfiltration of collected data via HTTPS POST
file_indicators: Presence of long hex-encoded strings in main entry files
Functions that decode and immediately eval code
References to require('os'), require('dns'), require('fs'), require('https') in combination with obfuscated code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to unknown or hardcoded domains
POST requests with hex-encoded payloads in the body
Connections initiated at import-time or immediately after package load
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for packages containing long hex-encoded strings that are decoded and executed via eval, especially in main entry files. Monitor for Node.js processes that, upon import or execution, immediately collect system/user information and make outbound HTTPS POST requests with encoded payloads. Flag packages that use obfuscation and dynamic code execution, particularly if they access sensitive directories or environment information without clear user intent.
